channelTitle: You've probably pulled this weed out of your garden, Grandma June kept it on purpose
hook: You've probably yanked this weed straight out of your garden, but Grandma June always kept a patch of it on purpose.
remedy: As a classic piece of old-fashioned home wisdom, the broad leaves of the common plantain weed, crushed or chewed to release their juice, were pressed onto bug bites, bee stings, and small scrapes as an old-fashioned way to calm the itch and soothe the skin.
steps: Pick a few clean plantain leaves (the broad, ribbed weed, not the banana-like fruit)
Crush or chew the leaf briefly to release its juice
Press the crushed leaf directly onto the bite, sting, or scrape and hold in place for a few minutes
caution: Only use leaves you're certain are plantain weed and free of pesticides. See a doctor for a serious allergic reaction, a deep wound, or a sting that swells significantly.
cta: Had you heard of using plantain leaf this way, or is this a first for you? Let Grandma June know in the comments.
